purpose: Upgrade selected behavioral mechanisms from source-inspection evidence to source-plus-test/spec evidence without promoting implementation-specific claims into universal truth.

records.supported_mechanism: belief state is updated from observations while preserving a distinct state/history representation
test_observations: tests assert a bounded belief/history length
a new observation updates the latest belief element while prior history is retained
the prior belief object is asserted unchanged
invalid belief initialization/update shapes raise errors
records.ceiling: The tests validate this implementation's belief updater behavior; they do not prove any particular belief model is correct for an external task.

records.supported_mechanism: retrieval/search visibility is reader-snapshot dependent and explicit refresh/currentness checks matter after index changes
test_observations: tests assert a reader becomes non-current after writer changes
opening a fresh reader exposes updated/deleted documents
currentness can change across commit/close boundaries
source documentation requires openIfChanged/new reader to see index changes
records.ceiling: Freshness of the index view does not establish truth or quality of indexed content.

records.supported_mechanism: declared dependency/export boundaries can be checked against actual cross-module references
test_observations: allowed in-boundary and exported calls are asserted warning-free
classified forbidden cross-boundary references are asserted to produce warnings
configuration can explicitly relax incoming/outgoing checks
dirty-reference exceptions are themselves checked for unnecessary use
records.ceiling: Tests demonstrate enforcement behavior for the library; they do not prove a given boundary design is architecturally correct.

records.supported_mechanism: bidirectional parser-printer contracts surface values that cannot be faithfully represented on the reverse path
test_observations: valid parse and print behavior are both asserted
printing an out-of-contract value explicitly raises a round-trip expectation failure
a reversible rational parser-printer is tested in both directions
records.ceiling: Round-trip equivalence is appropriate only where reconstructability is contractual; canonicalization/lossy transforms need a different declared contract.

records.supported_mechanism: branchable transaction history can preserve divergent states and test merge/common-ancestor behavior explicitly
test_observations: tests construct multiple named branches from a common root
branch-specific transactions are preserved and validated
merge strategies and constraint-violation cases are included in the test list
records.ceiling: This supports branch/history semantics, not the repository's broader performance claims.

behavioral_use: These records justify stronger confidence that the transferred mechanisms are implemented and tested in their source systems, while behavioral benefit for Sol still requires E18/E20/E25/E26/E27 execution.
